title: How do we draw both customer counts on one line graph?
description: A shop counts the customers who visit and the customers who buy, from Monday to Sunday. The video draws both counts as two lines on one grid, each with its own mark, the same way as the line graph in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: two counts for the same days need two lines on one grid, each with its own mark. Watch for students who join the two counts into one line.

video_script.why: The child has drawn one line graph from a column graph and now draws two counts on one grid.
video_script.substitution: Set the days and a scale, put a dot for each count, join each count separately, then read both lines.
video_script.anchor: the book's table of customers who visit a shop and customers who buy, over a week
video_script.payoff_line: both lines peak on Sunday, and purchasing stays below visiting every day

final_answer.value: Two lines on one grid; both peak on Sunday, purchasing stays below visiting
final_answer.spoken: two lines on one grid, both lines peak on Sunday, and purchasing stays below visiting every day

never_show: one joined line for both counts
maths_rules: scale: 0 to 40 in steps of 5, because the largest count is 35; days along the bottom
purchasing is below visiting each day: 10 < 16, 8 < 19, 7 < 10, 11 < 14, 12 < 20, 16 < 22, 26 < 35
the largest visiting count is 35 and the largest purchasing count is 26, both on Sunday
video_script.design: One idea: two counts, two lines, one grid. The table stays beside the grid; each count gets its own shape and colour.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='shop'/>A shop counts its customers every day for one week. Some customers only visit. Others visit and also buy something.
<bookmark mark='table'/>The table gives both counts, from Monday to Sunday.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we show both counts on one line graph?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko appears at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: an empty grid with the days along the bottom; a circle mark and a square mark shown in a key

marks.days: an empty grid appears with the seven days along the bottom
marks.two: two coloured lines are sketched on the empty grid
marks.marks: a circle mark and a square mark appear in a key

narration: <bookmark mark='days'/>A line graph joins dots in the order of the days.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two counts need two lines on one grid.
<bookmark mark='marks'/>Each line gets its own shape of mark, so we can tell the two lines apart.

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number of customers who visit on each day, and the number who buy.

marks.find: the task is written under the table

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to draw both counts as lines on one grid.

narration: <bookmark mark='days2'/>Step one, put the days along the bottom.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>Put the number of customers up the side, from zero to forty in steps of five.

narration: <bookmark mark='vis'/>Step two, mark a dot for each day's visiting count. These are sixteen, nineteen, ten, fourteen, twenty, twenty two and thirty five.
<bookmark mark='vis2'/>Join the dots in the order of the days.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: purchasing dots (square marks) 10, 8, 7, 11, 12, 16, 26, joined in order as a second line

marks.buy: seven square dots appear, one for each day

narration: <bookmark mark='buy'/>Step three, mark a different shape for each day's purchasing count. These are ten, eight, seven, eleven, twelve, sixteen and twenty six.
<bookmark mark='buy2'/>Join these dots as a separate line, and do not join the two counts together.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check each dot against the table, day by day, for both lines

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the graph against the question.
<bookmark mark='check2'/>Read each dot's height and match it with its number in the table, for both lines.

beats.on_screen: Answer: two lines on one grid; both lines peak on Sunday; purchasing stays below visiting every day

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>We get two lines on one grid. Both lines peak on Sunday, and purchasing stays below visiting every day.
